title: WTO | Tariff and trade data
content:
The WTO website offers many options for researching members' customs duty rates and their levels of exports/imports. The new
WTO Tariff & Trade Data platform
provides enhanced access to official tariff and trade figures for over 150 economies. It includes bilateral trade datasets, time series views, and reports on export
and import patterns by product and trade partner.

The platform aggregates official information about applied tariffs and import data notified by WTO members to the WTO's Integrated Data Base (IDB), and bound duties
(agreed maximum tariffs) and other commitments recorded in the WTO's Consolidated Tariff Schedules (CTS) database. This data is supplemented by the WTO Analytical
Database (ADB), which integrates WTO sources such as regional trade agreements (RTA) and external partners such as the International Trade Centre (ITC), UN Comtrade
The platform follows a multi-tiered update schedule, with updates ranging from daily to monthly, depending on the data source.
The Integrated Database (IDB) contains time series of the tariffs applied by WTO members and acceding economies to imports from other WTO members. Data are provided
at the most detailed product level (usually the eight to ten digit product level or tariff line code). The database also contains import statistics, including the
value and volume of imports by country of origin and by tariff line.
Consolidated Tariff Schedules Database
The Consolidated Tariff Schedules (CTS) Database contains the agreed maximum tariffs that WTO members can impose on imported products from other WTO members and, if
applicable, their specific commitments in agriculture (domestic support, export subsidies and tariff quota information).
The WTO Analytical Database is a comprehensive tariff and trade flow database that consolidates most-favoured nation (MFN) bound, applied and preferential tariffs,
together with trade flow data from various sources. These include Integrated Database (IDB) tariffs and import data, Consolidated Tariff Schedules (CTS) bound rates,
preferential commitments from the WTO Regional Trade Agreements (RTA) Database, ITC data from the World Tariff Profile datasets as well as trade data from UN Comtrade
All data is standardized into time series at the Harmonized System subheading level. The result is a single, ready-to-query dataset showing — by product,
partner and year — the legally bound duty, the MFN applied tariff, the preferential tariff a partner could claim, and the value of merchandise that crossed the
border, all expressed in the same version of the HS. The data can be accessed through the
WTO Tariff & Trade Data Platform
The World Tariff Profiles is an annual co-publication by the World Trade Organization, the International Trade Centre, and the United Nations Conference on Trade and
Development. This comprehensive statistical yearbook provides detailed information on tariffs and trade, as well as non-tariff measures. It covers over 170 countries
and customs territories, including WTO members and non-WTO members for which the most recent tariff data is available. It is designed to facilitate comparisons across
countries/territories, between various sectors, and specifically, to allow for comparison between bound and applied tariffs for WTO members.
Customs codes and product categories
Products in the databases are identified using the World Customs Organization's internationally agreed "Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System"
The HS codes are standard up to six digits, the most detailed level that can be compared internationally. Beyond that, WTO members are free to use their own
definitions according to their individual requirements.
The Harmonized System is regularly reviewed and amended. Detailed information on the evolution of the HS across its various editions can be found in
Multilateral Trade Negotiation (MTN) product categories
MTN categories are  key product grouping used by the WTO to classify goods, particularly in the "World Tariff Profiles". These categories encompass 22
primary product groups, which are further subdivided into 72 sub-categories. The relationship between the six-digit HS codes and the WTO MTN product categories is
available for download from the Tariff and Trade Data Platform.
